vf.p: I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately with my job. I work 60-hour weeks and my manager keeps piling on more tasks. I just don't know how much more I can take.
My best friend of 10 years stopped talking to me out of nowhere and I can't figure out why. I keep replaying every conversation we had recently and I feel sick about it.
I'm thinking about quitting my stable job to open a bakery. Everyone thinks I'm being stupid. Maybe they're right? I'm terrified but also kind of excited.
I got passed over for a promotion I'd worked toward for two years. A colleague who started after me got it instead. I'm trying not to be bitter but I feel completely deflated.
I was laid off on Monday after eleven years at the same company. They gave me twenty minutes to clear my desk. I keep telling people I'm fine and I'm really not.
My new team lead criticised my work in front of everyone in the standup. I've barely been able to open my laptop since. I know I'm overreacting but it stung badly.
I've been freelancing for a year and I still panic every time a month starts with no work booked. I can't tell if this is normal or if I've made a huge mistake.
I finally quit the job that was making me miserable and now I just feel unmoored. Everyone congratulated me and I mostly feel scared.
My dog of 14 years died on Tuesday. I know people say it's just a pet, but I've been crying every day and I feel ridiculous about it.
My dad was diagnosed with early-stage dementia last week. He seems like himself most days and then suddenly he isn't. I don't know how to be around him without falling apart.
It's been a year since my mother died and everyone seems to think I should be over it. Some days I still reach for the phone to call her.
My grandmother is in hospice and I live six thousand miles away. I can't afford to fly back again and I'm terrified she'll die while I'm arguing with myself about it.
We lost the pregnancy at fourteen weeks. We'd already told everyone. Now I have to keep telling people and every time feels like it happens again.
My partner and I have been arguing about the same thing for months and last night they said maybe we should take a break. I feel like the ground disappeared.
I found out my sister has been talking about my divorce with the whole extended family. I feel humiliated and I don't know how to face any of them at Christmas.
My husband and I haven't had a real conversation in weeks. We're perfectly polite to each other and that somehow feels worse than fighting.
I ended a four-year relationship two months ago because I knew it was right, and I still cry in the car most mornings. I don't understand why it hurts this much if it was correct.
My roommate moved out without telling me she was going. I came home to half the furniture gone and a note. I don't even know what I did.
I keep getting ghosted after three or four dates. I've stopped telling my friends about anyone because I can't stand the sympathy face.
My teenage son told me he hates me last night and slammed his door. I know it's normal but I sat on the stairs and cried for an hour.
My parents keep asking when I'm going to give them grandchildren and I've had two miscarriages they don't know about. Every dinner is an ambush.
I had to put my mother in a care home this week. She asked me why I was abandoning her and I don't think I'll ever unhear it.
My daughter didn't invite me to her graduation. She said it was a small ceremony. I found out from Facebook that her father was there.
I'm the only one of my siblings who does anything for our parents and nobody has ever acknowledged it. I'm so tired and I feel guilty for being tired.
I got a chronic illness diagnosis last month. The doctor was matter-of-fact about it and I walked out to my car and just sat there. I don't know who I am with this yet.
I've been in physical therapy for eight months and I still can't run. I keep being told to be patient and I am so far past patient.
My test results came back inconclusive again and I have to wait another three weeks. The waiting is worse than any answer would be.
I've gained a lot of weight since my surgery and I avoided my own birthday party because I didn't want anyone to see me. I feel pathetic writing that down.
I had a panic attack on the train yesterday and had to get off two stops early. I've been taking the long way to work ever since and I'm ashamed of it.
I failed my licensing exam for the second time. I studied for eight months. I don't know if I can put myself through this again.
My manuscript got rejected by the twelfth agent this week. I've started to think the kind thing would be for someone to just tell me I'm not good at this.
I've been sober for three years and last weekend I drank. Nobody knows. I feel like a fraud and I'm terrified of telling my sponsor.
Everyone in my cohort has published and I haven't. I sit in seminars nodding and feeling like I tricked my way in here.
I'm 34 and I just moved back in with my parents. I know it's temporary and practical and I still feel like I've failed at being an adult.
I bombed the presentation I'd prepared for three weeks. My mind went blank in front of everyone. I've replayed it maybe two hundred times since.
I moved to a new city six months ago for work and I still haven't made a single real friend. I go home every night and just sit there. I'm starting to wonder if something is wrong with me.
I spent my birthday alone last week. I told everyone I had plans. I'm not sure why I lied.
All my friends have kids now and the invitations just stopped. I don't blame them and it still feels like being slowly deleted.
I work fully remote and yesterday I realised I hadn't spoken out loud to another person in four days. It didn't feel dramatic at the time, which is what worries me.
My rent is going up 30% and I genuinely don't know what I'm going to do. I've run the numbers four times hoping I did them wrong.
I had to ask my younger brother for money this month. He said yes immediately and was kind about it and I've felt sick ever since.
I'm 41 with almost nothing saved for retirement. Every article about compound interest feels like it's written to punish me specifically.
I came out to my parents at Christmas and they changed the subject. They've never brought it up again. I don't know if that's rejection or something else.
I retired in March and I thought I'd feel free. Mostly I feel invisible. I don't know how to say that to anyone without sounding ungrateful.
My youngest left for university last month. I've cleaned the house top to bottom twice. It's very quiet and I don't know what I'm for now.
I've been in this career for fifteen years and I've realised I don't like it. It feels far too late to say that out loud.
I became a citizen last year and I still feel like a guest everywhere I go. I thought the paperwork would change something.
I didn't visit my friend in the hospital because I couldn't handle seeing him like that. He died on Thursday. I don't know what to do with this.
I reported a colleague for something serious and now the whole office has gone cold on me. I know I did the right thing and I feel completely alone in it.
I lost my temper with my kid over something tiny and saw him flinch. I've never felt worse about myself than I did in that second.
I said yes to being maid of honour and I resent every minute of it. She's my oldest friend and I feel like a terrible person.
I've been avoiding my best friend since her father died because I don't know what to say. It's been two months now and the silence has become its own problem.
I have a to-do list with 47 things on it and I've been staring at it for an hour without starting any of them. This happens most days now.
I check my email at 2am. I know that's not normal. I don't seem able to stop.
Every time my phone rings with an unknown number my chest goes tight. It's been like this since the hospital called about my mum last year.
I'm caring for my father, working full time, and my own health has gone completely to the bottom of the list. I don't see where the slack is supposed to come from.
I've been dreading a conversation with my landlord for three weeks. It would take ten minutes. I cannot make myself do it.
I got into the programme I wanted and I've been anxious ever since instead of happy. I keep waiting for them to realise they made a mistake.
I've been on a waiting list for therapy for seven months. Every time I call they say the same thing. I've started to feel stupid for still hoping.
My closest colleague resigned last week without telling me it was coming. We ate lunch together every day for four years. I feel oddly betrayed and I know that's unreasonable.
My divorce was finalised on Tuesday. I expected relief and instead I sat in the car park for forty minutes. Eleven years and it took four minutes to end.
The vet says it's time to let my cat go and I have to choose the day. I keep looking for reasons she might rally. I don't trust myself to decide this.
My son was diagnosed with dyslexia and I keep thinking about all the times I told him to concentrate harder. I can't stop replaying those conversations.
My partner has been drinking again and hiding it. I found the bottles this morning and I just stood there in the garage not knowing what to do next.
I was made redundant at 55 and I've had forty applications go nowhere. Nobody says it's my age. I've started leaving dates off my CV and I hate that I have to.
I failed my driving test for the fourth time. My instructor was kind about it, which somehow made it worse. I'm 29 and everyone I know just drives.
Our last round of IVF didn't work. We'd agreed it would be the last one either way. I don't know how to start living in the version of my life where this doesn't happen.
My daughter hasn't spoken to me in two years and I still don't fully understand why. I write her birthday cards I never send.
We're moving abroad for my husband's job and my mother is 84. Everyone keeps telling me it's a wonderful opportunity and I feel like I'm abandoning her.
I've had chronic pain for three years and the last consultant suggested it might be stress. I've started rehearsing how to sound credible before appointments.
I lost eleven thousand pounds to a scam that now seems obvious in hindsight. I haven't told my husband. I feel stupid and I feel worse for hiding it.
The house sale fell through two days before completion. We'd already packed. I've been sleeping badly and snapping at everyone.
My oldest friend just got the exact job I've been trying to get for two years. I said congratulations and meant it and also felt something ugly underneath.
I sent a client email to the wrong distribution list with a comment about their budget in it. That was Monday. I still feel sick every time I open my inbox.
My wife had a stroke in March and I've become her carer overnight. I love her and I miss the person I could talk to about this.
The baby is eleven weeks old and I haven't slept more than three hours at a stretch. I know this is normal and I feel like I'm coming apart anyway.
I went back to work after nine months of leave and it's like the job moved on without me. Everyone's very nice and I feel completely peripheral.
There's someone on my team who undermines me in every meeting, always just short of anything I could report. I've started dreading Mondays properly.
We've been long-distance for two years and last night we couldn't think of anything to say to each other. Neither of us has mentioned it today.
Everyone I graduated with owns a home and has a career and I'm still temping at 33. I know comparison is pointless and I do it constantly.
It's my brother's birthday today. He died four years ago and everyone seems to have forgotten. I don't know whether to say something or let it pass.
Since the divorce I go whole weekends without speaking to anyone. I've started going to the supermarket just to have somewhere to be.
I have to fly to my sister's wedding next month and I'm terrified of flying. I haven't told her because I don't want to make her day about me.
I got promoted into a role I'm not sure I'm qualified for and I've been reading old handovers at midnight so nobody finds out.
My parents are three hours away and I visit maybe twice a year. My dad's getting frail. I tell myself I'm busy and I know that isn't really it.
My PhD supervisor died suddenly last month. He was the only person who understood what my project was for. I don't know how to carry on with it.
The team went ahead with the launch project and nobody thought to include me. I found out from a calendar invite I wasn't on.
They found something on my scan and I have to wait eighteen days for the biopsy. I've been functioning normally at work and falling apart in the evenings.
My dog needs an operation that costs four thousand pounds and I genuinely cannot afford it. Working out what to do feels like a betrayal whichever way it goes.
My brother has borrowed money from our parents for years and I've never asked for anything. At Christmas my mother thanked him for being so helpful.
My husband and I are perfectly kind to each other and I don't think he's actually looked at me in about a year. I don't know how to raise that.
My father shouldn't be driving any more and he won't hear it. I keep imagining a phone call and then feeling awful for imagining it.
I chose medicine because my family expected it and I've been doing it for fourteen years. I think about leaving most weeks and I never do.
I've lived here for four years and I still don't have anyone I could call on a bad evening. I didn't think making friends would be this hard as an adult.
I'm a paediatric nurse and last month I stopped feeling anything at work. I used to cry after difficult shifts and now I just go home.
I haven't wanted to do anything in about six weeks. Not sad exactly, just flat. I keep waiting for it to lift on its own.
My mother-in-law told me I'd let myself go, in front of my children. My husband laughed. I haven't been able to stop thinking about it.
I turned down a job I wanted because I was scared, and they've since hired someone junior to me. I did this to myself and that's the part I can't get past.
My best friend is moving to Australia in six weeks. I'm genuinely happy for her and I've cried twice this week about it.
I found my old sketchbooks while clearing the loft. I haven't drawn anything in nine years and I couldn't tell you why I stopped.
I've been offered a job in another city. More money, but I'd leave everyone I know. I keep going back and forth and I can't tell what I actually want.
My lease is up in two months and I'm weighing renewing versus moving closer to work. Both options have real downsides and I've been putting off deciding.
I'm considering going back to school part-time at 38. It's a lot of money and time. I'm curious whether people usually regret this.
A friend asked me to be a reference for a job I don't think she's ready for. I haven't answered her yet and it's been three days.
I've been invited to my ex's wedding. We ended things amicably. I genuinely don't know whether going would be mature or masochistic.
My sister wants to host Christmas this year and it always ends in an argument. I'm trying to decide whether to say something in advance or just let it play out.
I've been thinking about getting a dog but I travel for work about one week a month. I keep talking myself into it and then out of it.
My team wants to switch to a four-day week and I'm the only one who isn't sure. I don't want to be the person blocking it.
I was asked to give a toast at my father's retirement dinner. Our relationship is complicated. I've written four drafts and thrown them all away.
I'm debating whether to tell my manager I'm job hunting. She's been good to me and I don't want to burn anything, but I also don't want to blindside her.
My neighbour's tree drops leaves all over my garden every autumn. It's mildly annoying and I can't work out whether it's worth mentioning.
I've been offered a promotion that's mostly management. I like the work I do now. Everyone says you should take it when it's offered.
My partner wants to move in together and I think I want that too, but I keep finding reasons to delay the conversation.
I have two weeks of leave I have to use or lose. I can't decide between visiting family or actually resting, and I feel slightly guilty about the second one.
A close friend has started a business and asked me to invest. I can afford it. I'm not sure how to think about mixing this with the friendship.
I've been asked to speak at a conference in my field. It's a good opportunity and public speaking has never gone especially well for me.
My book club has drifted into being a wine night and I actually wanted to read. It feels petty to raise it.
I'm thinking of cutting back from full-time to four days. The money works out but I worry about how it'll be read at work.
My flatmate is lovely but never cleans. It's not a crisis, it's just constant, and I've started keeping score in my head.
I was left a small inheritance and I can't decide between paying down the mortgage or finally taking the trip we've talked about for years.
We're choosing between two primary schools for our daughter. One is closer, one has better results. I keep going round in circles on it.
A friend borrowed money eight months ago and hasn't mentioned it since. It's not a large amount and I can't work out whether raising it is worth the awkwardness.
My GP is confident about the diagnosis and something about it doesn't sit right with me. I'm weighing up whether asking for a second opinion is reasonable or just difficult.
The house is too big for us now that the kids have gone. Downsizing makes obvious sense on paper and I keep finding reasons to postpone looking.
I never learned to drive and I'm 41. It feels faintly embarrassing to start now, and it would genuinely make life easier.
There's a school reunion next month. I wasn't especially happy there and I'm oddly curious. I've been putting off replying for a fortnight.
A junior colleague asked me to mentor her. I'd like to and my own workload is already unmanageable. I don't want to say no badly.
I'm considering dropping to part-time so I can finish my degree. The maths works out and I'm not sure how it would land with my manager.
My siblings want to sell our parents' house and I'm the one who grew up in it. Practically they're right. I keep stalling on the paperwork.
We've talked about getting a second dog. The first one is settled and elderly and I can't tell whether it would be lovely for her or unfair.
I'm frustrated — my Python script keeps throwing a KeyError on line 40. I've already printed the dict keys and checked for typos. What else should I look at?
Really annoyed at this: my laptop fan runs constantly even when nothing's open. Is there a way to find out what's actually using the CPU?
This is driving me mad — my sourdough comes out dense every time. I'm using a starter that doubles reliably and a 75% hydration dough. What am I likely getting wrong?
I've been stuck on this for hours and I'm losing patience. How do I merge two branches in git when both have modified the same file?
My car makes a grinding noise when I brake and it's stressing me out. What are the likely causes and roughly what should a repair cost?
Ugh, my houseplant keeps dropping leaves despite watering it weekly. It's by a north-facing window. What should I check?
Getting nowhere with this — my wifi drops out every evening around 8pm. Router is three years old. Where would you start diagnosing?
I'm irritated that no one warned me about this: what's the actual difference between a Roth and a traditional IRA, in plain terms?
My spreadsheet formula returns #REF! after I deleted a column and it's maddening. How do I fix the references without rebuilding the whole sheet?
Slightly exasperated here — how do I get red wine out of a wool rug? It's been about two hours.
I keep messing this up. What's the correct order of operations for seasoning a cast iron pan from scratch?
This has been bugging me all week: why does my bread machine loaf collapse in the middle? Recipe is standard white.
Frustrating problem — my bike chain slips under load in the higher gears. Chain and cassette are about a year old. What's the usual culprit?
I'm fed up with rewriting this paragraph. What's a clear way to explain standard deviation to someone with no statistics background?
Annoyingly, my phone battery went from all-day to half-day in about a month. Is there a way to see what changed?
I've read three tutorials and I'm still confused, which is aggravating. What does a Docker volume actually do, and when do I need one?
My tomatoes split every year and it's disheartening. I water them daily in summer. What causes that?
Bit exasperated — what's the difference between a mortgage's APR and its interest rate? Every explanation I find contradicts the last one.
This keeps happening and it's tedious: my printer says it's offline even though it's connected to wifi. What's the usual fix?
I'm running low on patience with this recipe. How do I stop a custard from curdling when I temper the eggs?
This is maddening — my photo backup says it completed but half the albums are missing on the new phone. Where should I look first?
Getting fed up: my radiator is cold at the top and hot at the bottom. Is bleeding it the fix or is it something else?
I've lost an hour to this. What's the actual difference between git rebase and git merge, and when would I want each?
Irritatingly, my bread dough won't rise in a cold kitchen. Is there a reliable way to proof it without a proving drawer?
This keeps tripping me up. In Excel, why does VLOOKUP return N/A when the value is visibly there in the column?
Frustrated with my own French — what's actually the most effective way to get from reading fluently to speaking without freezing?
Annoying problem: my laptop won't connect to the office projector over USB-C but works fine at home over HDMI. What's the likely cause?
I've asked three people and got three answers, which is aggravating. What does an ETF expense ratio actually cost me in practice?
Bit exasperated — my basil dies within two weeks every single time, on a bright windowsill, watered every other day. What am I doing wrong?
This has beaten me twice now. How do I safely replace a light switch, and how do I confirm the circuit is actually dead first?
